sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28-12-2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 28-12-2022 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner and his wife were returning from temple and stopped the vehicle for dinner at Ganesh Grand Hotel, after having dinner at about 8.30 p.m. they were standing left side of the hotel to cross the Bengaluru- Doddaballapura road at Bashettihalli, in front of Ganesh Grand Hotel, at that time the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 came from Bengaluru towards Doddaballapura at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner who was standing on left side of the road and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Manipal hospital,
Doddaballapura, wherein he took first aid treatment thereafter he was shifted to Raksha Health Care, Rajankunte, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and also undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.75,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment and attendant expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 44 years and was doing Business and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, petitioner is still under treatment and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. Inspite of service of summons, respondent No.1 - owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.

After service of summons, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of package policy to the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124 and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the policy was valid at the time of accident.

Further contended that,
there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that, the rider of the offending motor cycle was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident and also the involvement of the offending motorcycle in the said accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident due to rash and negligent act of riding of Honda Activa motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 and as a result, he sustained injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioners as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much & from whom?
4. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Further examined two witnesses as PW.2 &3 and got marked Ex.P.14 to 17 and closed their side evidence.
On perusal of the exhibits marked in this case the PW1 produced Ex.P13 documents and PW2 produced Ex.P.14 to P.16 documents.
Thereafter the PW3 produced 2 documents which are also marked as Ex.P.16 and 17 instead of P.17 and P.18.

To avoid the confusion office is directed to make necessary correction in the document No.1 produced by the PW3 which is marked as Ex.P16, by correcting the same as Ex.P.18 by virtue of the observation made in this judgment.
The respondent No.2 examined examined its official as RW-1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and 2 and closed their side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.

The learned counsel for the petitioner relied on the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.202104/2024 between the Branch Manager, ICICI Lombard Nibhaya Vadde Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. V/s Pooja & others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

for the following:-

sentences.text: 3 8. That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR and complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, seizure mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet and notice and reply U/Sec.133 of MV Act, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 10.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of the first information given by one A.C.
Lalitha who is the mother of petitioner.
The first informant has alleged about the negligence of the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4.
As per the spot mahazar and sketch marked at Ex.P3 & 4 the accident spot is within 3 feet from the edge of the road and also the accident spot is in front of Ganesh Grand Hotel.

Thereby it is evident that the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 came to the extreme left side and was negligent in his riding, as such he was unable to control his vehicle and dashed against the petitioner.
Thus the contents of Ex.P3 & P4 establishes the negligence of the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.

Further, the Ex.P.6 being the IMV report discloses that there were no damages found on the offending Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39- HG-4124.
10.

The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The PW.1 was cross-
examined at length by denying the negligence of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Thereby the contention of the respondent No.2 in respect of contributory negligence of the petitioner cannot be accepted.
11. Ex.P8 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.

It is very important to note that if the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was in a controllable speed and if he was not negligent he could have controlled his vehicle before dashing the petitioner.

This shows the gross negligence of the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.
12.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124.
13.
The charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 is came to be filed on the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39- HG-4124 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC and Sec.180, 181 of MV Act.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;
2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.

4 Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP- 39-HG-4124.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 28-12-2022 which is caused by the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2 and 3:
These two issues are taken together for common discussion as these issues are connected each other in respect of the entitlement of the claim made by the petitioner.
20. As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP- 39-HG-4124.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

5 a) PAIN AND AGONY:-

entities.text: Vageesh Bhushan A.C vs Gali Bhargav Teja
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner has alleged that at the time of accident he was aged about 44 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P13 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 13.05.1978.
The accident took place on 28-12-2022.
Hence as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 44 years.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Raksha Health Care from 28-12-2022 to 01-01-2024 for a period of 5 days and sustained Right distal radius fracture.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P12,
amounting to Rs.1,13,580/-.
These bills are supported by the medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P15 and Ex.P14 advance bills.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.1,13,600/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was doing business and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.15,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2022.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 petitioner was admitted to Raksha Health Care.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500 X 4 months = Rs.62,000/-
during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., working as Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho And Dental Center as PW.3, through him recent examination report and X-ray are marked at Ex.P17 & P18.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained left distal radius fracture, PW.3 has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability left arm at 35% and to the whole body at 12%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross- examination.
According to the petitioner he was doing business and suffered with fracture of left distal radius.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 10% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 14 X 10% =Rs.2,60,400/- which is the total loss of future income.

6 e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;

entities.text: Vageesh Bhushan A.C vs Gali Bhargav Teja
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to Raksha Health Care Hospital and taken the treatment and also underwent surgery.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner admitted to Raksha Health Care as per Ex.P11.
There is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.
But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges Rs.5,000/- in total as he was inpatient for a period of 5 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.3 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.60,000/-.
But has not produced any estimation.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.40,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: Liability:-

The respondent No. 1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 and taken contention that the rider of the offending motor cycle was not having valid licence at the time of accident.

In this regard the official of respondent NO.2 insurance company examined its official as RW-1 and produced the Ex.R1 &
2.
22.
The Ex.R2 is the copy of policy wherein it shows that the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was insured with them from 04.01.2021 to 03.01.2026.
The date of accident is 28-12-2022.
As such as on the date of accident the offending Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39- HG-4124 was duly insured with respondent No.2 - insurance company.
23. The respondent No.1 is the RC owner of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 has not appeared before this tribunal.

24. Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?

Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.2 insurance company that owner has handed over the offending Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 to a person who has not having valid driving license.

To establish the said fact, the respondent No.2 initially relied on Ex.P8 charge sheet wherein Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.180, 181, 187 of IMV Act are invoked against the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124.
On perusal of the Ex.P8 the rider of the said offending Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid licence at the time of accident to drive the said vehicle.
25. The respondent No.1 owner not appeared by denying the contents of charge sheet in this regard.
Thereby the respondent No.2 insurance company discharged its burden to hold that the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
26. There is no dispute that at the time of accident the vehicle was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

As per Ex.R2 it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.

In this case,
the respondent No.1 owner of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 not contested the petition by adducing any evidence by showing that the rider was having driving license at the time of accident.
27. The next aspect to be pondered upon now is, what is the effect if the rider of the offending vehicle not possessing a driving license at the time of accident.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 insurance company successfully discharged the burden and proved the violation of conditions of policy as the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
Hence, next point needs to be considered is to whom the liability has to be fastened.

MFA No.7018-2023 C/w. MFA No.2658-2024 between M/s. TATA AIG General Insurance Company Limited V/s. Manjunatha and others, wherein it is held as follows;
"15.

entities.text: TATA AIG General Insurance Company Limited V/s. Manjunatha and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is relevant to note here that since the owner of the offending vehicle is present before the Court and is participated even before the tribunal, the liability will have to be fastened as against the owner of the offending vehicle.

However, learned counsel for the owner contends that in view of there being policy valid as on the date of occurrence of accident, the question of pay and recover in the present case would not arise, which in my opinion, cannot be accepted".

By relying on the above quoted judgment, the evidence of the petitioner as well as RW.1 clearly set out the aspect regarding the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid driving licence at the time of accident and the respondent No.1 being the owner with full knowledge handed over the insured vehicle to the driver to ride the same without driving licence hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
29. By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

As per Ex.R2 it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.
30. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 has not appeared and not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the unauthorised person to drive the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 is a fundamental breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the partly affirmative and Issue No.3 is answered in the affirmative by holding that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as discussed above.

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,76,000/- (Rupees Five lakhs seventy six thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization.
The petition against respondent No.2- insurance company stands dismissed.
The respondent No.1-owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the compensation awarded, the entire amount awarded to the Petitioner, shall be released to him on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
17. In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 28-12-2022 which is caused by the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124 which belonging to respondent No.1.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
To establish the said fact, the respondent No.2 initially relied on Ex.P8 charge sheet wherein Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.180, 181, 187 of IMV Act are invoked against the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG- 4124.
On perusal of the Ex.P8 the rider of the said offending Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid licence at the time of accident to drive the said vehicle.
Thereby the respondent No.2 insurance company discharged its burden to hold that the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.
As per Ex.R2 it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.
In this case,
the respondent No.1 owner of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 not contested the petition by adducing any evidence by showing that the rider was having driving license at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 insurance company successfully discharged the burden and proved the violation of conditions of policy as the rider of Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 was not having valid DL at the time of accident.

But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

30. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 has not appeared and not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.
Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the unauthorised person to drive the Honda Activa bearing No.AP-39-HG-4124 is a fundamental breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.

9 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,76,000/- (Rupees Five lakhs seventy six thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization.
The petition against respondent No.2- insurance company stands dismissed.
The respondent No.1-owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the compensation awarded, the entire amount awarded to the Petitioner, shall be released to him on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
